idiom_name: JMS standard grouping on the JVM; kotlinx.coroutines Channel / Flow for in-process sequences
implementation_notes: On the JVM the broker implements the pattern (Jakarta Messaging JMSXGroupID and JMSXGroupSeq), so Kotlin reuses it with ordinary property syntax; in-process, kotlinx.coroutines gives ordered delivery for free - a Channel is FIFO and hands each element to exactly one receiver, and Flow.buffer()/channelFlow() place a bounded channel between producer and collector with an explicit onBufferOverflow policy, which replaces the sequence-number structure while both ends share the process. The header plus reassembly form is still required across processes on transports without groups, for example Kafka ConsumerRecords.
pitfalls: Channel.RENDEZVOUS and UNLIMITED change back-pressure but not ordering; UNLIMITED turns the group buffer into an unbounded memory risk.
A Channel is confined to one process and guarantees nothing about the wire, so never drop the sequence fields in a distributed flow.
Cancelling the collector while parts are buffered silently drops the group; use structured concurrency so the group either completes or fails visibly.
